change: a practice lab is no longer gated, because no teacher has a switch that could open it
_context: Reported 2026-09-09 with two screenshots. He unlocked Quiz and Lab on his 1.2
row, waited five minutes, signed in and out of his student profile, and the
lab was still shut. The student page said both halves of it in adjacent
sentences:
'This one is practice. It checks your work on the page and records nothing.'
'Your teacher has not opened this lab yet.'
The Lab chip on 1.2 is 1.2-auth-lab, 'Read the login log', graded, filed at
unit-1/1.2. His students were opening ap-cyber-unit-1-lesson-2-lab, which
mounts 1.2-lab, 'Find the tournament code', UNGRADED and filed at unit-4/4.3.
The title on his screenshot is the tournament one, so the two are certainly
different labs.
An ungraded lab gets no course_manifest row on purpose. seed-manifest.js:
'a manifest row is a denominator, and a denominator for work a student cannot
do marks the whole class down for a reason no teacher can see on screen. A
practice lab is playable and scores nothing, so it gets no row.'
No row means no gradebook column, which means no switch anywhere on the
assignments board. So the only thing that can ever close that lab is a WIDER
row written about something else, and nothing can reopen it.
THE CLASS DEFAULT IS NOT THE MECHANISM. The first reading of this blamed
quiz_lock_default, and the suite caught it: DEFAULT_GATED is {quiz, exam}, so
the class default has never touched a lab. It is a unit or lesson lock, which
is the ordinary way a term starts. That fact is now asserted rather than
assumed, because a wrong mechanism is a wrong answer to the teacher even when
the fix is right.
NOT FIXED HERE, and it is the other half: lesson 1.2 links to a lab the server
files at 4.3, while 1.2's own graded lab sits on a different page. That is a
storefront wiring question and it needs a sheet and a human's judgement about
which lab belongs on that lesson.

checks.name: practice ungated, graded unchanged, and the source is the manifest
checks._why: The risk is not that practice labs open, it is that this becomes 'labs are no longer gated'. Section 2 re-asserts every way a real lab is still shut: an explicit row, a unit lock, and the anonymous cross-class refusal. Section 3 is the only part that can tell spec.graded from the manifest row, because seed-manifest builds one from the other and they agree in production.

checks.name: the ladder and both enforcement paths are untouched
a teacher preview and the four caller shapes still resolve as they did
checks._why: This adds a branch ABOVE the teacher carve-out shipped earlier today, so the earlier fix has to survive it.

checks.name: an independent decision table agrees with the route on all 40 caller and gate combinations
checks._why: Written from the rules rather than from routes/labs.js. Rule 0, a lab with no gradebook column is not gated, is stated in the same list as the ladder rules and one arrangement removes the manifest row so the new branch is compared rather than only the ladder underneath it.

checks.name: the settle fix from earlier today still settles
checks._why: Its section 1 drives the LAB route, so the new branch sits above it. It seeded no manifest row and went red until the fixture was corrected, which is the finding worth keeping: every suite that drives this route now has to model a lab a teacher could actually gate.

checks.name: the lab-gate mutation battery, which is what caught this branch weakening a guard
checks._why: CI found what my own gate did not. The new branch sits above the anonymous rule, and smoke/lab-gate.js seeded no manifest row for OPEN_LAB, the second lab that exists solely to keep 'anonymous is refused' from meaning 'every lab is refused'. That lab short-circuited open and the assertion stopped testing the anonymous rule at all. The battery still went RED on that mutation, but on a DIFFERENT assertion, which is the signal that a rule has gone hollow rather than that a suite has broken. It also caught a mutation anchor that my edit had shifted, so one mutation had silently stopped running. It is a suite here rather than a mutation entry because it already is a mutation harness; mutating it under the gate tests the gate, not the route.

checks.name: read spec.graded instead of asking the manifest
checks._why: Looks identical in production, because seed-manifest builds lab rows from labSpecs.graded(). It is wrong the moment a lab gets a hand-listed manifest row, which the seeder already does for some, and it would be wrong silently. Only section 3 can see it.
checks.expect_failure: a GRADED lab whose row is missing goes ungated

checks.name: match the manifest row on course alone
checks._why: A lookup that ignores item_id finds SOME row for the course and calls every lab gated, which restores the reported bug while looking like a working check. Course-only and item-only lookups both pass the graded case.
